 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:22.02.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.3119/2009 ON THE FILE OF THE I ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSE JUDGE, MACT, BANGALORE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the M.V.Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short)
challenging the judgment and award passed by the MACT (SCCH-11), Bengaluru in M.V.C.No.3119/2009 dated 22.02.2012.
2.

The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 04.02.2009 at 9.00 p.m. near Kuvemplu Circle, Outer Ring Road, Jalahalli Main Road, Bangalore the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.HR-38-J-7812 drove it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA03-HB-8190.
As a NC: 2023:KHC:40727 result, the claimant who was the rider of the motor cycle suffered grievous injuries.
3. Thereafter, the claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Act claiming compensation of Rs.20 Lakhs.

The tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,15,000/- to the claimant with interest by fastening the liability on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.
Being aggrieved by this judgment and award, the claimant is before this court by way of this appeal seeking enhancement.
4. Heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the records.
5. The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the income taken by the tribunal is on the lower side.
He would contend that the tribunal instead of Rs.5,000/- has taken the income at Rs.4,000/- per month.

sentences.text: As such, he would seek for enhancement of the compensation awarded to the claimant by the tribunal.
6. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 would support the judgment and award passed by the tribunal.

7. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, there is no serious dispute of the fact that the claimant has suffered injuries in the road traffic accident and he was the rider of the two-wheeler.
The liability is also not in dispute.
The appeal is restricted only to the extent of enhancement that too regarding the monthly notional income taken by the tribunal.

The tribunal by considering the notional income as Rs.4,000/- per month has awarded the total compensation of Rs.3,15,000/- under various heads as under:
 Pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/-
 Loss of happiness and future Rs.50,000/-
 amenities  Loss of income during treatment Rs.16,000/-
 period  Incidental charges Rs.24,000/-
 NC: 2023:KHC:40727  Medical expenses Rs.59,800/-
 Loss of future income Rs.1,15,200/-
. The claimant has suffered fracture of right tibia.
The implants were also inserted and considering these aspects, the tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering, which does not call for any interference.
Further, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head loss of amenities, which is also reasonable one.

Under the head of incidental charges,
Rs.24,000/- was awarded and under the head of medical expenses a sum of Rs.59,800/- was awarded, which is based on material evidence and the compensation awarded under these heads does not call for any interference.
9.
The tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.4,000/- per month.
The accident has occurred in the year 2009.
This court is consistently taking the income at Rs.5,000/- per month pertaining to the accidents that occurred in 2009.
Hence, the income NC: 2023:KHC:40727 taken by the tribunal is on the lower side.
If the notional income is taken Rs.5,000/-, then, the income during laid up period would be Rs.20,000/- (Rs.5000x4).
The tribunal has considered the disability to the extent of 15% by taking the notional income at Rs.4,000/-.
There is no dispute regarding the multiplier adopted i.e., '16'.

Considering the income as Rs.5,000/-, the loss of future income would Mr Mohammed Ashfaq Ali vs Mr Karpal Singh on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46225681/
3 work out to Rs.1,44,000/- (Rs.5000x12x16x15/100).

sentences.text:
Hence, under the head of loss of future income,
the claimant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.1,44,000/-.

As such, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation under various heads as under:
 Pain and suffering -Rs.50,000/-
 Loss of happiness and amenities -Rs.50,000/-
 Loss of income during -Rs.20,000/-
 Laid up period  Incidental charges -Rs.24,000/-
 Medical expenses -Rs.59,800/-
 Loss of future income -Rs.1,44,000/-

Hence, claimants would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,49,000/- as against Rs.3,15,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC:40727 awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the claim petition needs to be allowed in part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The claim petition is allowed in part.
(ii) The claimant is held entitled for a total compensation of Rs.3,49,000/- as against Rs.3,15,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

(iii) The enhanced compensation of Rs.33,000/-
shall carry interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till payment.
(iv) The respondent No.2 - insurer is directed  to deposit the entire enhanced compensation with accrued interest within a period of six weeks from today before the tribunal.
(v) The entire enhanced compensation shall be released in favour of the claimant.
